newsitem.title: USA: U.S. likely to appeal ruling halting deportations.
newsitem.headline: U.S. likely to appeal ruling halting deportations.

text.p: The Justice Department is likely to appeal against a ruling halting deportations of Nicaraguans and other immigrants who claim the United States has improperly denied them residency, officials said on Thursday.

Department officials said lawyers still were studying the ruling handed down by a federal judge in Miami on Wednesday and that no decision had yet been made on whether to go to a federal appeals court based in Atlanta.

But one official privately said she assumed the case would be appealed, especially in view of the possible significance of the ruling, while another official said he would be surprised if an appeal was not filed.

U.S. District Judge James Lawrence King ruled that Nicaraguans and other immigrants affected by a new immigration law would be "irreparably harmed" without an immediate order preventing the government from sending them home.
"No one will be deported," King ruled from the bench, adding that the restraining order took effect immediately.
Asked at her weekly news briefing about the decision, Attorney General Janet Reno said, "We are reviewing (it) at this point."

At issue in the case was a controversial new immigration law passed by Congress last fall, several provisions of which went into effect April 1. Lawyers for the immigrants argued the Immigration and Naturalisation Service improperly applied the law retroactively to dismiss appeals by immigrants.
The judge halted deportations indefinitely until the case could be heard and decided on the merits.
